text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer says carmaker will not close any further plants through the year 2000.
-- Government launches reform of a 1937 banking sector decree setting a rigid framework for working hours and opening days.
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade sees the state-owned bank as having recovered, and nearly ready for privatisation.
-- Trade Minister Jean-Pierre Raffarin presented to cabinet meeting yesterday details of law setting limits to supermarkets in urban areas.
-- EU reactions to further Credit Lyonnais bailout plans to be unveiled in two weeks.
-- Finance Minister calls for a European uniformised VAT tax system to prevent cross-border fraud.
-- Renault carmaker posts over five billion francs loss for 1996, Prime Minister Alain Juppe calls for industry regrouping.
-- Cap Gemini computer services group buys 50.6 percent stake in Portugal's Geslogica.
-- LVMH posts a 1996 profit down 9 percent at 3.68 billion francs.
